# Cognition Therapeutics Reports Financial Results for the Third Quarter 2026 and Provides Business Update


– Management conference call at 8:30 a.m. ET today –


November 05, 2026 06:00 ET


PURCHASE, N.Y., Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) —[Cognition Therapeutics, Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=37CvQUlbHJ5KYjaRx7mkMKAWljW3sAYFO7iW4dahOyoaBTpYfcvpUVtr4tXHmwEbycF_mG69D4wpZLYUpz3mfqWIeO1Hnb3bh0No-gzuDuc=) (NASDAQ: CGTX), a clinical-stage company developing product candidates that treat neurodegenerative disorders (the “Company” or “Cognition”), today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update.


Lisa Ricciardi, Cognition’s president and CEO stated, “The work we conducted with the Office of Neuroscience at the FDA during 2026 culminated in the development of a trial protocol for a planned registrational study of zervimesine (CT1812) in people with dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). We are now evaluating our plans for manufacturing, site selection, and patient recruitment.


“At the same time, we are working with our collaborators at the Alzheimer’s Clinical Trial Consortium (ACTC) to prepare for the conclusion of the Phase 2 START Study in people with MCI and early Alzheimer’s disease,” Ms. Ricciardi added. “Top-line results from START are anticipated in the second half of 2027 and will inform our plans for zervimesine in Alzheimer’s disease.”


**Business and Corporate Highlights**


- Aligned with FDA on primary and key secondary endpoints for Phase 3 trial of zervimesine in DLB.
- Began development of Phase 3 protocol with insights from panels of people with DLB and caregivers.
- Received issued patent with natural expiration of 2045 from United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) covering a novel crystalline form of zervimesine.
- Received notice that poster developed with Alzheimer’s Clinical Trials Consortium (ACTC) has been accepted for presentation at Clinical Trials in Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) annual meeting. Presentation highlights efficiencies achieved in Phase 2 START study by using p-Tau 217 assay during screening.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results**
Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash equivalents as of September 30, 2026 were approximately $31.5 million, and total obligated grant funds remaining from the National Institute of Aging, a division of the National Institute of Health were $18.2 million. The Company estimates that it has sufficient cash to fund operations and capital expenditures into the fourth quarter of 2027.


Research and development expenses were $5.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.8 million for the comparable period in 2025. The increase in research and development expenses was driven by higher trial activities with contract research organizations and professional fees.


General and administrative expenses were $2.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.6 million for the comparable period in 2025. The decrease in general and administrative expenses was driven primarily by lower professional fees and compensation.


The Company reported a net loss of $4.1 million, or $(0.04) per basic and diluted share for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $4.9 million, or $(0.06) per basic and diluted share for the same period in 2025.

**About Cognition Therapeutics**
[Cognition Therapeutics, Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=37CvQUlbHJ5KYjaRx7mkMKAWljW3sAYFO7iW4dahOyqz0mrzxYJnUyKKyl1uiG8CsPCkBROeL2XC8zU1IryJ63D05AmsH_8yKecHOv2jT0o-TVNuMUZT846Nl5EaCYv2) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to helping millions of families seeking effective treatments for devastating neurodegenerative diseases through the development of novel, accessible therapies. The company has led pioneering research into the underlying mechanisms of degenerative nerve disorders. Our scientific approach builds on well-established biological pathways and translates across indications in which toxic oligomers drive disease progression, offering potential in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), Alzheimer’s disease, geographic atrophy, Parkinson’s, among others. The company’s lead candidate, zervimesine (CT1812), is an investigational once-daily oral therapy that has demonstrated promise in Phase 2 clinical trials in DLB and mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease. Backed by nearly $200 million in National Institutes of Health and related foundation grants, Cognition Therapeutics continues to advance clinical research in its efforts to bring forth solutions that meet patients where they are and reduce caregiver burden. Learn more at[cogrx.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=wKB996hi3SCSRZChDITU633MKvXcEaGLgGJP9d0C92aKXgYKXj2k0uChYKk8iAUflTdk9mxbAVMNuj3QQK5-ZQ==) .


**About Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB)**
Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is a progressive, fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by neuropsychiatric, cognitive, and motor deficits. It is the second most common cause of dementia. It is estimated that 1.4 million Americans are living with DLB. However, research shows that more than half are never diagnosed during their lifetime, suggesting that the prevalence of DLB could be substantially higher. There are no approved drugs to slow the decline of DLB or treat the symptoms that are core features of the disease.


**About Zervimesine (CT1812)**
[Zervimesine](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=VFBRVYXGJe-JVECVmsTmpc62eeqHNdtX5BNOSrgu5HX5gXjls0A7Yf7VPMjh_jKo9pRrqILimJwpEuXuAAl9SRx-TnCR6FU614PW6Y90p_w=) (CT1812) is currently being studied in the Phase 2 START Study ([NCT05531656](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=vZCloFQ8a1rOkSLnKG4ueFD_FVkZVbVML0E6pUIYdvyXtaN3Xn-B0gpjKxceDhthJv-sqhjKtW6d4W4GILNhmsN1rM2I9BBS-uPTahVNmXLuHa1g3iQ5crs2w7_tF9Fb) ) in patients with MCI and early Alzheimer’s disease. Phase 2 clinical studies have concluded in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease, and geographic atrophy secondary to dry AMD. In the Phase 2 SHIMMER study in DLB ([NCT05225415](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=vZCloFQ8a1rOkSLnKG4ueDikiYnme0LXz7B9CGcCpp8De7TlPP28k6RE4e5vXVs6DTwTMs6o3GwHfzRy4gz_eKZc-srFU2s4kyfmcU8JuQPOpa0tW2mqLPRu-BL3ywUm) ), zervimesine was shown to slow DLB disease progression, resulting in a slowing of neuropsychiatric, cognitive, motor, and functional symptom progression. Zervimesine has been generally well tolerated in clinical studies to date.


Zervimesine is protected by a robust intellectual property portfolio including a recently issued composition of matter patent covering a novel crystalline form that has a natural expiration of 2045. The USAN Council has adopted zervimesine as the United States Adopted Name (USAN) for CT1812.
